messages:
ashley: FYI canary perf alert — int8 profile p95 jumped ~18% after merge 4f2a9b3, happened ~10:02 UTC. Blocking rollout.

matt: seeing the same on our smoke traces. p50 mostly fine, tails are bad.

sara: can you paste the perf summary from the profiler?

ashley: pasted quick flame from the canary node:```
hotspots:
  dequant_memcpy: 42%
  kernel_dispatch: 21%
  kv_cache_lookup: 8%
  batch_coalesce: 6%
```

devon: wait merge 4f2a9b3 was the kernel selector change that prefers "fused-quant->fp32" variants when batch_size > 1 to avoid extra kernel launches. Maybe the selector is choosing a path that forces a dequant memcpy on the hotpath for our INT8 runtime.

ashley: yep. profiler shows a memcpy from int8->fp32 buffer before kernel, then kernel expects contiguous FP32, so we pay the copy per request.

matt: interesting — on smaller sequences the fused kernel is faster, but for long seqs + prefix cache we get a cache-unfriendly copy. Could be an alignment/padding interaction.

ci-bot: CI perf guard flagged regression on commit 4f2a9b3: p95 +17% on quant-smoke suite. See CI run https://ci.internal/runs/5923

sara: assigning a bisect. I'll run a binary search between 4f2a9b3^ and parent to confirm.

devon: quick local bisect I ran narrowed it to the kernel selection heuristic change + the padding alignment tweak in the same PR. If you force old selector we don't hit the memcpy.

ashley: can we add a short-term fix: revert the selector heuristic and keep the padding tweak? or add a fastpath that avoids memcpy when kv cache shows prefetched contiguous blocks?

matt: revert LGTM as emergency. Also we should add a telemetry counter for "dequant_memcpy_bytes" and a per-request flag when fused path used.

prod-bot: Rollout blocked by: performance regression alert (p95 +18%). Action required: rollback or mitigation.

sara: opening a revert PR now (WIP: revert/selector-heuristic-4f2a9b3). Will run canary once reverted.

ashley: also adding replicable micro-benchmark for long-sequence + kvcache scenario to CI so future selector changes run against it.

devon: note for postmortem: tradeoff was intended (reduce kernel launches) but under-prefetching + padding led to extra copies. We need cost model: kernel_launch_cost vs memcpy_cost for typical seq distributions.

matt: agreed. I'll sketch a simple cost estimator and a unit test matrix for seq_len x batch_size x kvcache_hit rate.

ashley: thanks folks — will monitor CI. ping if canary still reports anything after revert. :thumbsup:
